title: Mark Hurdlestone; or, The Gold Worshipper

title: 'The Song of the Lower Classes'

literary_form: Chartist song (published in the Northern Star)
meter_and_prosody: Verse. Verse: the line and stanza follow the conventions of the genre, and the poem is written to be read aloud. The author's characteristic manner is ballad and song forms with heavy refrain.

Prose of the industrial novel: the documentary description of the mill, the mine, the street and the strike, the dialect of the workers set against the language of the masters, and the plot built on the collision of the two nations. title: Woman's Wrongs
description: Published in 1853 and Jones's contribution to the early feminist argument in England: a series of lectures on the wrongs of women under English law and in the industrial system. It is a prose work of 1853 by Ernest Jones; it belongs to Chartism and the Condition-of-England Novel and it is catalogued here under Review Essay and Quarterly Argument; Lecture and Popular Address.
plot_or_argument: Jones examines the position of women in the factory, the marriage law, the property law and the labour market, and argues that the emancipation of women is inseparable from the emancipation of labour.
narrative_structure: An essay in sections, the argument stated, the evidence quoted, the objection answered and the judgement delivered, in the compass of the quarterly review. The printed lecture: the address to the audience, the repetition and the triadic climax, and the peroration, retaining the shape of the delivery.
meter_and_prosody: Prose. Prose of the quarterlies: the long periodic sentence of argument, the quotation and the set-piece judgement, the division into numbered or titled sections, and the assumption of a general reader of the reviewing class. The work is a pamphlet, a single argument in a short compass. The text is the printed lecture, retaining the spoken address. The author's characteristic manner is ballad and song forms with heavy refrain.
